slots.practicalActivity: Build a small synthetic customer table in pandas (age, tenure_months, monthly_spend, plan, region, plus a churned label), then fit a LogisticRegression with the fit/predict/score pattern on 2 numeric columns. Loop over a DummyClassifier baseline, the logistic regression, and a RandomForestClassifier using the exact same fit/predict/score calls, printing predict_proba for 3 rows to see the estimator/transformer/predictor roles in action.
slots.deliverable: A script that builds a synthetic customer DataFrame and trains 3 different scikit-learn classifiers (dummy baseline, logistic regression, random forest) with identical fit/predict/score calls, printing each model's held-out accuracy next to the baseline's.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a ColumnTransformer that scales 2+ numeric columns and one-hot-encodes 1+ categorical columns on your synthetic customer table, then wrap it with a LogisticRegression inside a single Pipeline. Fit the pipeline on raw, unprocessed data and run cross_val_score on it, then compare against a deliberately leaked version where you fit the ColumnTransformer on the full dataset before cross-validating, to see the leakage inflate the score.
slots.deliverable: A working Pipeline combining a ColumnTransformer and a classifier, with printed cross_val_score output showing the leak-free score next to the inflated, leaked score from fitting preprocessing outside the pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit the full ColumnTransformer+LogisticRegression pipeline from the previous slot, save it to disk with joblib.dump, then in a separate script load it back with joblib.load and call .predict on 5 new raw rows to confirm the restored pipeline reproduces identical predictions to the original in-memory model.
slots.deliverable: A saved .joblib pipeline file plus a second script that loads it and prints predictions on 5 held-out rows that exactly match the original model's predictions.

slots.practicalActivity: On the held-out test set from your saved churn pipeline, compute accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC AUC by hand with sklearn.metrics, then plot the ROC curve with RocCurveDisplay.from_estimator and mark where the model's default 0.5 threshold sits on the curve.
slots.deliverable: A printed accuracy/precision/recall/F1/ROC AUC table plus a saved ROC curve plot for the real trained pipeline, with the default threshold's point marked.

slots.practicalActivity: Generate a confusion matrix with ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator for your trained classifier, then sweep the decision threshold across 5 values (0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7) using predict_proba, printing precision and recall at each threshold to see the tradeoff.
slots.deliverable: A saved confusion matrix plot at the default threshold, plus a 5-row threshold-sweep table of precision and recall at each threshold.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit a LinearRegression and a RandomForestRegressor on a numeric target (e.g. a synthetic price or spend column), then compute and compare MAE, RMSE, and R-squared on the held-out test set for both models, writing one sentence per metric explaining what it means in the original units of the target.
slots.deliverable: A printed MAE/RMSE/R-squared comparison table for 2 trained regression models, plus a 3-sentence explanation of what each metric means for the specific target variable.

slots.practicalActivity: Run 5-fold StratifiedKFold cross_val_score on your pipeline scoring F1, reporting the mean and standard deviation (never a single number), then plot a learning curve with sklearn.model_selection.learning_curve to diagnose whether the model would benefit from more training data or less complexity.
slots.deliverable: A bar chart of the 5 fold F1 scores with the mean line drawn, plus a learning-curve plot with a written one-paragraph diagnosis of underfitting, overfitting, or a need for more data.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Evaluating Models: produce one comprehensive model report for your churn pipeline combining every tool from this chapter — cross-validated F1 and ROC AUC with their spread, a confusion matrix at the default threshold, a precision/recall threshold sweep, and a learning curve.
slots.deliverable: A one-page model evaluation report combining cross-validation results, a confusion matrix, a threshold sweep table, and a learning curve for one real trained model.

slots.practicalActivity: Tune a RandomForestClassifier with GridSearchCV over a 3-hyperparameter grid (e.g. n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_leaf), fit it with cv=5, and print best_params_, best_score_, and the full cv_results_ sorted by rank_test_score to see every combination tried, not just the winner.
slots.deliverable: A printed best_params_ and best_score_ result plus a cv_results_ table sorted by rank showing at least the top 5 and the single worst parameter combination.

slots.practicalActivity: Re-run the same hyperparameter search problem from the previous slot using RandomizedSearchCV with n_iter=10, comparing the total number of model fits and the resulting best_score_ against the full grid search, to see whether random search found a comparably good answer with far fewer fits.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison table of total fit count and best_score_ for grid search versus random search on the same model and parameter space.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately repeat GridSearchCV several times while adjusting the grid based on peeking at test-set scores, to see the test score creep upward dishonestly; then redo it correctly, tuning only against cross-validated scores and touching the test set once. Finish by comparing your two top candidate models' per-fold cross-validated scores to judge whether their difference is real or just noise.
slots.deliverable: A written before/after demonstration of the validation-set-overfitting mistake, plus a fair per-fold comparison of 2 candidate models showing whether their score gap is larger than the fold-to-fold spread.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Tuning Models: tune a full preprocessing-plus-model pipeline end to end with GridSearchCV, check cv_results_ for a winner sitting at the edge of the grid and widen it once if needed, then report one final, untouched test-set score for the winning configuration.
slots.deliverable: One complete hyperparameter-tuning project producing a final tuned pipeline, its best_params_, and a single honest test-set score reported exactly once.

slots.practicalActivity: Build or load a dataset with a rare positive class (around 5-10% minority rate), print the real class balance with value_counts(normalize=True), then compare a DummyClassifier predicting only the majority class against a real classifier, showing the dummy's high accuracy but zero recall on the minority class.
slots.deliverable: A printed class-balance percentage plus a side-by-side accuracy/recall comparison of a dummy classifier and a real classifier on the same imbalanced data, proving accuracy alone is misleading.

slots.practicalActivity: Using imbalanced-learn, compare RandomUnderSampler, RandomOverSampler, and SMOTE on the same imbalanced dataset. First resample the whole training set before cross-validating (the wrong way) and note the inflated recall, then wrap the sampler inside an imblearn.pipeline.Pipeline so resampling happens only within each training fold, and compare the honest recall/precision.
slots.deliverable: A recall/precision comparison table for 3 resampling strategies, plus a documented before/after pair showing the leakage from resampling outside the pipeline versus the honest in-pipeline result.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit a classifier with class_weight="balanced" on the same imbalanced dataset and compare its default-threshold precision/recall against the unweighted model. Then introduce missing values into 2 numeric columns and, inside a ColumnTransformer pipeline, compare a plain median SimpleImputer against SimpleImputer(add_indicator=True) to see whether a missingness-indicator column recovers predictive signal.
slots.deliverable: A comparison table of class-weighted versus unweighted precision/recall, plus a second table comparing cross-validated AUC for plain imputation versus add_indicator=True.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Imbalanced & Messy Data: combine the chapter into one leak-free pipeline on a single imbalanced, messy dataset - SMOTE (or class weights) applied only inside cross-validation folds, missing-value imputation with an indicator column, and a final honest test-set evaluation comparing at least 3 strategies.
slots.deliverable: One consolidated imblearn Pipeline handling imbalance and missing data together, with a final comparison table of at least 3 strategies scored on the same held-out test set.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a synthetic telecom-style churn table (tenure, monthly_charge, contract type, support_tickets, autopay) and frame the project as a business action in one sentence. Compare a dummy baseline, logistic regression, and random forest with cross-validated ROC AUC, evaluate once on the test set, then rank test customers by predicted risk and report what percentage of actual churners the riskiest 20% call list captures.
slots.deliverable: A trained churn pipeline plus a written business summary: the top-20% call list's real churn rate versus the base churn rate, and the percentage of all churners it captures.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a synthetic product or housing price table with at least 4 numeric/categorical features. Compare a mean-prediction baseline against LinearRegression and RandomForestRegressor with cross-validated MAE and RMSE, then plot predicted versus actual price for the held-out test set to visually check for systematic over- or under-prediction at the high and low ends.
slots.deliverable: A trained price-prediction pipeline plus a predicted-vs-actual scatter plot with a written note on where the model is most wrong.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a synthetic transaction table with a rare fraud label (around 1-3% positive rate). Apply the leak-free imbalance techniques from Chapter 4 inside a single pipeline, evaluate with a precision-recall curve rather than accuracy, and report, at one chosen decision threshold, how many flagged transactions are false positives per true fraud caught.
slots.deliverable: A trained fraud-detection pipeline with a precision-recall curve, plus a written cost-tradeoff statement at one chosen threshold (true frauds caught versus false alarms).

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page model card/README for one of your three Chapter 5 projects (churn, price, or fraud), documenting the problem framing, the data and preprocessing choices, the real cross-validated and test metrics you obtained, and known limitations or caveats a stakeholder should know before trusting the model.
slots.deliverable: A README.md model card for one completed project, containing the project's real computed metrics and an explicit limitations section.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Build and Defend a Prediction Model

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real prediction problem (classification or regression) using a public dataset of your choosing. Write one sentence stating the business action the model enables, split off and seal a test set you will not touch again until the wrap-up, and define at least 2 numeric success floors (e.g. a minimum ROC AUC or MAE and a baseline to beat) before writing any model code.
slots.deliverable: A written capstone framing document with the problem statement, a sealed held-out test set file, and explicit numeric success criteria.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one leak-free ColumnTransformer-plus-Pipeline for your capstone dataset. Compare at least 4 candidates (a dummy baseline plus 3 real models, e.g. logistic/linear regression, a random forest, and a class-weighted or resampled variant if the target is imbalanced) with stratified cross-validation on 2 metrics, tune the strongest candidate with RandomizedSearchCV or GridSearchCV, then save the final winning pipeline with joblib.
slots.deliverable: A saved .joblib capstone model plus a model-comparison table (at least 4 candidates, cross-validated mean and spread on 2 metrics) showing which one won and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Open your sealed capstone test set exactly once, compute the final honest test metrics against the success floors from the kickoff, read the winning model's coefficients or feature importances to explain its top drivers, and write a 1-page portfolio presentation covering the problem, approach, final metrics, and what you'd try next.
slots.deliverable: A portfolio-ready write-up with the one-time final test-set metrics, a feature-driver explanation, and a "what I'd try next" section, ready to drop into a GitHub repository.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can take a raw, messy, real-world dataset and build a production-style scikit-learn pipeline - preprocessing, cross-validated model comparison, hyperparameter tuning, and honest handling of class imbalance and missing data - then defend the model's metrics and limitations in a documented, portfolio-ready project.
